recommendation: Keep the audit commit and make no source change for FHIR-5201. Do not change cardinality or restore an absolute separate-instance rule without a new PA decision.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive PA DSTU1 change request asking whether managingOrganization and period should be tightly coupled or whether multiple managing organizations should be allowed; final resolution requested guidance on transfers and multiple organizations having their own EpisodeOfCare instances.
initial_application: No issue-keyed FHIR-5201 commit was found. The likely application was March 2015 EpisodeOfCare ballot reconciliation, especially f659c3fbc16870414aac80f798d75afcb5480bf8, which added the multiple-organization transfer section and period/status notes that later refactors preserved.
additional_context: FHIR-5208 depends on FHIR-5201 for the period clarification. Later FHIR-20612 refined the original absolute separate-instance wording into the current primary-managing-organization model, so current source should keep the non-absolute 'may have their own EpisodeOfCare' guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the active source already satisfies the issue: managingOrganization is the primary responsible organization, period is the interval for that responsibility, and the narrative covers transfer of care and other organizations' tracking instances.

related_jiras.note: Sister DSTU1 EpisodeOfCare period clarification that explicitly applies FHIR-5201's guidance.
